texts.li: No rain has fallen on {FACTION}'s country for two months. The streams above {PLACE} have dried to strings of pools, the wheat is standing white in the fields, and the herders are driving their animals farther every day to find water.\n\nThey're calling it {NAME}. If the rains don't come soon, it will be a hungry winter in {PLACE}.

[theirLowtech] Upriver, in {FACTION}'s country, the wells are failing one by one. At {PLACE} they are carrying water from a spring two hours' walk away, and the elders have started the old prayers for rain.\n\nThe herders have already begun driving their animals downriver, toward the colony.

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s reservoir at {PLACE} is down to a muddy bowl, and the pumps are pulling air. Water is rationed by the bucket, the crops are being let go field by field, and the herders are trucking their animals anywhere there's grass.\n\n{NAME}, their traders call it, and there's no end in sight.

[summer] "Dust," said the trader from {PLACE}, and tipped a boot out at the gate to show it. It hasn't rained in {FACTION}'s country since the spring, the fields are cracking open, and the people there have started calling the summer {NAME}.\n\nAt {PLACE} they watch the sky all day. It stays blue.

summaries.li: {FACTION}'s country is drying out: their herders will come looking for water, their caravans come less often, and heat waves are likelier. Help now will be remembered. If the rains don't come, a famine may follow.

texts.li: [river] Herders of {FACTION} have driven their animals down from the dry country, and they ask leave to water them at the colony's stretch of the river for a few days. The animals are thin and lowing, and the herders not much better.\n\nThey can pay {COUNT} silver, or owe the colony a favor.

[!river] A boy of {FACTION} has run ahead of the herd to ask: may they water their animals at the colony's wells for a few days, and graze the land beyond the fields? Behind him, the dust of the herd is already on the road.\n\nThe herders can pay {COUNT} silver, or owe the colony a favor.

li.label: Let them water the herds, as neighbors
li.outcome: The herders bring their animals down at dusk, and stay out of the fields as they promised. Their thanks will reach {PLACE} before they do.

li.label: Let them, for {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: The head herder counts out the silver slowly, and only then whistles the animals down to drink.

li.label: Keep them away
li.outcome: The herders are turned back at the boundary and drive the herd on, looking for water somewhere else.

texts.li: {FACTION} mean to dig a new well at {PLACE}, deeper than any they've dug before, and they don't have anyone who knows rock. They've heard {A_nameDef} does.\n\nThey ask whether {A_nameDef} would come and tell their diggers where and how. Or, if the colony would rather, {COUNT} silver would hire a well-digger from the coast.

[theirHightech] {FACTION} want to sink a new borehole at {PLACE}, and the drilling crew they hired has never worked this kind of rock. They've asked whether {A_nameDef}, who has, would look over the site and the logs for a day. Or the colony could put {COUNT} silver toward a better crew.

li.label: Lend them {A_nameDef} for a day
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went over the ground at {PLACE} with their diggers and showed them where the rock would give. They struck water two days later.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} found them the best spot there was, and they dug for a week. The well is deep and damp at the bottom, and gives about a bucket an hour.
li.deed: lent {A_nameDef} to dig a well at {PLACE}

li.label: Pay for a well-digger ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: A rider takes the silver from the gate in a locked box. A well-digger will be on the road to {PLACE} before the week is out.

li.label: It's their well
li.outcome: The rider goes home to {PLACE} with the colony's regrets.

texts.li: {FACTION} have given up the first fields at {PLACE} for lost and are rationing what's left. Their rider asks for {COUNT} portions of food, any kind, to stretch the stores until the rains come, and porters will follow to fetch it if the colony agrees.\n\nThey can pay something. They would rather pay the colony than the grain dealers.

li.label: Send {COUNT} food
li.outcome: Porters from {PLACE} come up for the food and go home bent under it. It will keep the town going a while longer.
li.deed: sent food to {PLACE} in the drought

li.label: Sell it at a fair price
li.outcome: {FACTION}'s porters come for the food and pay the usual price for it at the gate, counting the silver out on an upturned basket.
li.deed: sold food to {PLACE} at a fair price

li.label: Nothing to spare
li.outcome: The rider is told the colony can't spare it. If the drought comes this way, the colony will need every sack.

texts.li: The rain came at last, three days of it, soaking and steady. At {PLACE} people stood out in it with their faces up. {NAME} is over.\n\n{FACTION} got through it, with help from the colony, and they know exactly how much.
[well] The new well at {PLACE} is still running sweet now that the rain is back, and {FACTION} have named it after the colony.\n\n{NAME} is over.

li.chronicle: {NAME} broke at last; {FACTION} remember the colony's help.

texts.li: Late but heavy, the rains came back to {FACTION}'s country. {NAME} cost them a harvest, and {FACTION} remember the colony's share in getting through it.

li.chronicle: {NAME} broke, and the colony had done its share.

texts.li: The rains came too late for {FACTION}'s fields. {NAME} is over, but the harvest is gone with it, and the storehouses at {PLACE} are empty.\n\nHunger is coming to the region, and it won't stop at {FACTION}'s borders.

li.chronicle: {NAME} broke too late, and hunger followed.

texts.li: {NAME} is over, and {PLACE} lost a harvest and a good many animals to it.\n\nWhen {FACTION} talk about who stood by them that year, the colony doesn't come up.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ran its course; the colony kept to itself.

texts.li: [!noenemy] {FACTION} and {ENEMY} have agreed to build a road between their towns, and the surveyors' stakes run right past the colony. Work gangs from {PLACE} are already clearing the line.\n\nTheir foreman came up to the gate to say good day, and to ask where the colony draws its water so the gangs won't foul it.

[noenemy] {FACTION} are building a road out from {PLACE} toward the passes, and the line the surveyors staked out runs past the colony. The work gangs are already felling trees and laying the bed.\n\nWhen it's done, carts will come past every week, and the news with them.

[theirLowtech] {FACTION} are laying a stone road out of {PLACE}, the first in the region since the old empire's, and its line comes close by the colony. Oxen haul stone from the quarries, and the work gangs dig to the same two lines all day:\n\n"One for the ditch and one for the bed, and one for the stone that the carts will tread."

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s road crews are grading a new highway out of {PLACE}, and their machines can be heard from the colony on a still day. The survey line runs a few hundred paces from the gate.\n\nWhen it's done, the trucks will follow it.

summaries.li: Road crews and travelers pass by, and stranded carts are likelier. The colony can sell them timber, lend them a builder, and have a say in where the road runs. When it opens, traders will come more often.

texts.li: The road gang's foreman has walked up to the colony with a tally stick and a question. They're short of timber for the bridges and the culverts, {COUNT} logs at least, and the colony has a woodpile.\n\n{FACTION} will pay a fair price for it, or remember it as the colony's share of the road.

li.label: Sell them {COUNT} wood
li.outcome: The road gang's carts come for the timber, and {FACTION} pay a fair price for it at the gate.

li.label: Give it, as the colony's share
li.outcome: The road gang hauls the timber down from the gate with the colony's compliments. The foreman makes a mark for it on the tally stick.

li.label: We need our wood
li.outcome: The foreman nods and goes back down the hill to find timber elsewhere.

texts.li: The surveyors have two lines for the road past the colony, and they've asked the council to choose. One runs right past the gate, with all the traffic that brings, good and bad. The other swings around behind the hill, a day's work longer and much quieter.\n\nThe surveyors will go with the colony's word.

li.label: Past our gate
li.outcome: The stakes go in along the line past the gate. When the road opens, the colony will be on it.

li.label: Behind the hill
li.outcome: The surveyors move their stakes around behind the hill. The road will pass the colony by, near enough to walk to and far enough not to hear.

li.label: Let them decide
li.outcome: The surveyors are told to do as they think best. They choose the shorter line, past the gate.

texts.li: {FACTION}'s road gang has set the footing for the river bridge below the colony twice now, and twice the current has taken it. They've heard {A_nameDef} knows building, and ask for a day of {A_possessive} time at the crossing. They'll pay {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Lend them {A_nameDef} for a day
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent the day in the river with the road gang, and the footing {A_pronoun} set is still standing. {FACTION}'s foreman brought the silver up afterward, as promised.
li.deed: lent {A_nameDef} to bridge the river for {NAME}

li.label: We can't spare {A_objective}
li.outcome: The road gang will manage the crossing without the colony.

texts.li: The money ran out before the road did. {FACTION}'s gangs have gone home, and {NAME} ends in a heap of stones a mile past the colony.\n\nThe grass is already coming up through the gravel.

{NAME} is open, and it runs right past the colony's gate. The first carts are coming through now, and some of them will stop to water their animals and sell what they have.\n\nThere'll be more of them every season.

[bridge] {NAME} is open, over {A_nameDef}'s bridge and right past the colony's gate. The first carts are rolling over it now, and the drivers slow down to look at the work.\n\nSome of them will turn in at the colony's gate. There'll be more every season.

li.chronicle: {NAME} opened, running past the colony's gate.

texts.li: {NAME} runs behind the hill, as the colony asked, and opened this week. On a still night, the carts can just be heard.
{FACTION}'s carts are already on {NAME}. It isn't the colony's road, but the colony will use it.

{FACTION}'s priests have declared {NAME} at {PLACE}, a season when debts are forgiven, feuds are set aside and every traveler is fed. Pilgrims are already on the roads.\n\n{FACTION} hope their neighbors will keep the year with them, and they will see who does.

[ideology] The faithful of {FACTION} have proclaimed {NAME}, which comes once in a generation. At {PLACE} the shrines are open day and night, debts are being torn up in the square, and pilgrims are setting out from every corner of the region.\n\n{FACTION} have sent the same message to every neighbor. The year, it says, asks something of everyone.

[theirLowtech] Bells have been ringing at {PLACE} for three days. {FACTION}'s elders have declared {NAME}, as their grandparents did, and the old customs come with it: no hand raised in anger, no traveler turned away, and gifts for the poor at every door.

[theirHightech] {FACTION} have announced {NAME}: a season of public feasts, debts written off and pilgrimages to the shrine at {PLACE}. Their couriers have brought the notice to every settlement in reach, the colony included, printed on good paper and sealed.

summaries.li: Pilgrims and travelers pass far more often, and fewer raids come while the year lasts. {FACTION} hope the colony will feed pilgrims and keep the peace; generosity now is remembered.

texts.li: A long line of pilgrims bound for {PLACE} has stopped outside the colony's gate, as pilgrims in {NAME} do at every door on the road. They ask, as the custom is, for a bite of food, and they will give a blessing for it.\n\nAbout {COUNT} portions would feed them all.

[winter] Pilgrims bound for {PLACE} have come to the gate out of the cold, singing. In {NAME}, every door on the road is opened to them, and they ask the colony for food, about {COUNT} portions, and somewhere warm to sit before they go on.

li.label: Feed them ({COUNT} food)
li.outcome: The pilgrims eat at the gate, bless the colony in the old words, and go on toward {PLACE} singing.

li.label: Send them on
li.outcome: The pilgrims are sent on. The last of them stops at the gate to say the blessing all the same.

texts.li: In {NAME}, every household at {PLACE} is asked to forgive one debt. {FACTION}'s priests have written to ask the colony to do the same. A family of {FACTION} owes the colony {COUNT} silver from a bad year, and has never managed to pay more than a few coins at a time.\n\nIf the colony holds them to it, they can raise about half now.

li.label: Forgive it
li.outcome: Word goes to {PLACE} that the colony has forgiven the debt. The family sends a loaf of bread and their thanks.

li.label: A debt is a debt
li.outcome: The family raises half, all they can manage, and their eldest brings it up the road. {FACTION}'s priests aren't pleased.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been listening to the pilgrims on the road, and has asked the council for leave to keep {NAME} as they do: a day of silence and fasting, and the next given to whoever in the colony needs a hand.

[ideology] {A_nameDef} has been talking with the pilgrims of {FACTION}, and has asked to keep {NAME} with them in {A_possessive} own way: a day apart, in silence, and then a day of work done for others.

li.label: Let {A_objective} keep it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} kept a day of silence by the gate and spent the next doing other people's chores, and has been easier company since.

li.label: Not now, there's work
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} goes back to work, and keeps the year privately, in the evenings.

texts.li: {NAME} has ended with a feast at {PLACE}, and the priests of {FACTION} read out the names of those who kept it well. The colony was one of them.\n\nPilgrims on their way home have been stopping at the gate to say so.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ended; {FACTION} named the colony among those who kept it well.

texts.li: The last pilgrims of {NAME} have gone home past the colony's gate. {FACTION} remember that the colony kept some of the year with them.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ended; the colony had kept some of it.

texts.li: {NAME} is over. The pilgrims have gone home, the bells at {PLACE} have stopped, and the colony went on through it all as if nothing were happening.\n\n{FACTION} noticed.

li.chronicle: {NAME} passed; the colony kept to itself.

texts.li: {NAME} is dead, run down at a ford by riders of {FACTION}. The bandit lord had led {ENEMY}'s raiders on the roads around {PLACE} for as long as anyone remembers.\n\nThe band is coming apart. Some of its people want revenge or a new master. A few only want to stop running.

[theirLowtech] The head of {NAME} is on a spear over the gate at {PLACE}. {FACTION}'s warriors ran the bandit lord down in the hills after twenty years of raids, and {ENEMY}'s band has scattered into the woods.\n\nThe roads are safer already. They aren't safe yet.

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s militia raided the hideout of {NAME} three nights ago and broke {ENEMY}'s gang for good. The bandit boss died in the firefight.\n\nThe survivors are scattered across the region, and every farm for miles is barring its doors until they settle somewhere.

summaries.li: Stragglers from {ENEMY}'s broken band are on the roads: deserters asking for shelter, wounded strangers, buried loot coming to light. One of the band's lieutenants may try to gather the rest.

texts.li: One of the stragglers at the gate was never a bandit. Taken from a farm of {FACTION} years ago, they have been kept to cook and carry ever since, and the farm they were taken from is gone.\n\nThey ask the colony for a place.

[winter] Someone has walked out of the snow to the colony's gate, thin and ragged in a bandit's coat. They were {ENEMY}'s captive, not one of them, taken from {FACTION}'s country as a child. The band is gone, and they ask the colony for a place to stay.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: The colony makes room. The newcomer eats like someone who has never been sure of the next meal, and sleeps for a day and a night.
li.deed: took in a captive of the band

li.label: Feed them and send them on to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The colony feeds them and points the way to {PLACE}, where someone may still remember them.

texts.li: "Under a dead pine with a split in it you could put your arm through," says the man at the gate, one of {NAME}'s, and holds up a scrap of map. Only a few of the band knew where the bandit lord buried the hoard, and he is one of them. The map is the colony's for {COUNT} silver.\n\n{FACTION} would very much like to know where it is too. Most of what's in it was theirs.

li.label: Buy the map ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The map was true. A shovel and an afternoon turned up an iron box under the split pine, and what was in it belongs to the colony now.
li.riskOutcome: The map was true, as far as it went. Somebody else got there first: the hole was already dug, and the box was empty.

li.label: Send the map's owner to {FACTION}
li.outcome: The bandit is sent on to {PLACE} under guard, map and all. {FACTION} will dig up their own stolen goods, and they know who sent them the way.
li.deed: sent {FACTION} the way to the bandit lord's hoard

li.label: Send the bandit away
li.outcome: The bandit is sent off down the road, map and all, to try the next gate.

li.label: The last of {NAME}'s riders
li.text: One of {NAME}'s lieutenants has gathered what's left of {ENEMY}'s band, and wants a win to keep them together. The colony looks like one.

texts.li: {FACTION} are holding a feast at {PLACE} to mark the end of {NAME}, and every neighbor who suffered from the band is asked to send something for the tables. Their carts are going around the farms to collect it.

li.label: Send food for the tables (20 food)
li.outcome: A cart from {PLACE} collects the colony's share at the gate. At the feast, the colony's name is called out with the rest.
li.deed: sent food to the feast at {PLACE}

li.label: Send our good wishes
li.outcome: The colony's good wishes go to {PLACE} with a rider. They're received politely.

texts.li: The last of {NAME}'s band has scattered or come in from the cold, and the roads around {PLACE} are quiet for the first season in years. {FACTION} remember who helped them finish it.\n\nSome of the band's old fighters are looking for work, and not all of them are particular about what kind.

li.chronicle: After the fall of {NAME}, the roads around {PLACE} went quiet; {FACTION} remember the colony's part.

titles.li: A new master for the band

texts.li: The band of {NAME} didn't stay broken. One of the lieutenants has pulled the pieces back together under {ENEMY}'s banner, and the stories from the roads have started again.\n\nIt's too early to say how bad it will get.

li.chronicle: After the fall of {NAME}, a lieutenant pulled {ENEMY}'s band back together.

texts.li: The band of {NAME} is gone. A few are dead and a few are in {FACTION}'s cells, and the rest have scattered too far for any new leader to find.\n\nThe roads around {PLACE} are slowly filling with carts again.

li.chronicle: The band of {NAME} scattered after the bandit lord's fall.

texts.li: A sickness has gone through the herds of {FACTION}. At {PLACE} they are burning carcasses outside the town walls, and the smoke can be seen for miles. They call it {NAME}, and no one knows where it started.\n\nIt doesn't touch people. It takes their milk and their meat, and the oxen that pull their plows.

[theirLowtech] {NAME} has come to {FACTION}'s pastures: the cattle cough, then stagger, then lie down and won't get up. At {PLACE} every family has lost animals, and the herders are fighting over whose fault it is.\n\nThere'll be no meat to trade this season, and not much milk.

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s livestock inspectors have shut the markets at {PLACE}: a herd fever, spreading fast, with whole farms put down to stop it. They're calling it {NAME}, and asking every neighbor to keep their animals well away.

summaries.li: {FACTION}'s herds are sick: their traders come less often, and the colony's own animals are likelier to fall ill unless they're kept close. {FACTION} will ask for help, and for food.
[penned] The colony's animals are kept close to home, away from the sickness.

texts.li:
The notice from {FACTION}'s herd-masters is the same one every neighbor got:

Keep all beasts penned, off the common grazing and away from the roads, until {NAME} has passed. It goes by touch, and a short way on the wind.

Penning the colony's animals would mean a few weeks of hauling feed. It would also make them much less likely to catch it.

li.label: Pen them, and keep them close
li.outcome: The colony's animals are brought in close and kept there. It's more work, and it's safer.

li.label: Our animals graze where they always do
li.outcome: The colony's animals go on grazing as before. {FACTION} have been told, and aren't happy about it.

texts.li: Word has reached {PLACE} that {A_nameDef} knows animals as well as anyone in the region. {FACTION}'s herders are losing animals faster than they can bury them, and they ask whether {A_nameDef} would look at the sick ones and tell them what to do.\n\n{A_nameDef} would have to keep well apart from the colony's own animals for a few days afterward.

li.label: Send {A_nameDef} to help
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent two days among {FACTION}'s herds, sorting the sick from the well and showing the herders how to keep them apart. The losses at {PLACE} have slowed.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} did what could be done, and it wasn't much. The sickness had too long a start. {FACTION} thanked {A_nameDef} all the same, and meant it.

li.label: Keep {A_objective} home
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} stays with the colony's own animals. The herders of {PLACE} will have to manage.

texts.li: With half their herds dead or burned, {FACTION} are short of meat and milk at {PLACE}, and the winter stores are going faster than they should. A rider asks whether the colony can spare {COUNT} portions of food.\n\nTheir porters would come for it on foot. Most of their oxen are dead.

li.label: Send {COUNT} food
li.outcome: Porters come for the food on foot and go home with it on their backs. {PLACE} will eat this week.

li.label: Sell it at a fair price
li.outcome: {FACTION}'s porters pay the usual price at the gate and shoulder the sacks.
li.deed: sold food to {PLACE} at a fair price

li.label: Nothing to spare
li.outcome: The rider goes home empty-handed.

texts.li: The herds at {PLACE} are calving again, and the markets are open. {NAME} cost {FACTION} a great many animals, but it has passed.\n\nThey know who helped them through it.
[penned] The colony's animals came through {NAME} untouched, penned close to home, and the herds of {FACTION} are recovering. The colony kept its word about the pens, and the herd-masters noticed.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ended, and {FACTION} remember the colony's help.

texts.li: {FACTION}'s herds are thin and few now that {NAME} has passed, but they'll recover, and the colony helped where it was asked.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ended; the colony had lent a hand.

texts.li: {NAME} has run its course, and left {FACTION} with half the herds they had and a lean season ahead. The colony's animals grazed where they always had, and the colony sent nothing.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ran its course; the colony sent nothing.

texts.li: Three nights ago a light crossed the whole sky and came down in the hills past {PLACE}. It was a ship, {NAME}, and most of it is still there, broken across a valley. Salvagers of {FACTION} are already on their way.\n\nSo is everyone else with a truck and a cutting torch for a hundred miles.

[spacer] {NAME}, a freighter nobody in the region knew was up there, lost its orbit and came down in the hills near {PLACE}. The wreck is spread over a mile of ground, and the salvage rights are already being fought over in {FACTION}'s courts.\n\nIn the meantime, the scavengers are moving in.

[industrial] The sky lit up over {PLACE} one night, and in the morning there was a ship in the hills, broken in three pieces and still smoking. Its name is painted on the largest: {NAME}.\n\n{FACTION} have claimed it. Every scrap dealer in the region is going to try to take pieces of it home anyway.

summaries.li: Salvagers and scavengers crowd the roads to the wreck of {NAME}. Ship chunks and pods fall more often, components and steel are going cheap, and a survivor may turn up. Pirates may come for the wreck.

texts.li: A truck of {FACTION}'s salvagers has stopped at the gate on the way back from the wreck of {NAME}, loaded with steel plate and pulled components. They'd sell some of it to the colony, for {COUNT} silver, rather than haul it all the way home.

li.label: Buy a load ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The salvagers unload steel plate and a crate of components by the gate, count the silver twice, and drive off.

li.label: Not today
li.outcome: The salvagers drive on toward {PLACE}.

texts.li: A survivor of {NAME} is at the colony's gate, still in the rags of a ship's uniform. They climbed out of the wreck before the salvagers came and have been walking ever since.\n\nThey ask for water first, and then whether the colony takes in strays.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: The survivor is given a bed and a meal, and sleeps for most of two days. When they wake, they ask what work there is.

li.label: See to their hurts and send them to {PLACE} (1 medicine)
li.outcome: The colony patches the survivor up and puts them on the road to {PLACE}, where {FACTION} can see them home.

li.label: Send them on
li.outcome: The survivor is given directions to {PLACE} and walks on alone.

texts.li: {FACTION}'s salvagers have found {NAME}'s computer core intact, and none of them can read it. They've heard {A_nameDef} might, and offer {COUNT} silver for a day of {A_possessive} time at the wreck's data logs, brought up to the colony on a cart.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} have a look
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent the day bent over {NAME}'s logs with a pot of tea and came out of it knowing more about orbital freight than anyone needs to. The salvagers paid as promised when they came back for the core.

li.label: Not our business
li.outcome: The salvagers take the core away to someone else.

li.label: Scavengers from the wreck
li.text: Scavengers of {ENEMY}, who came for the wreck of {NAME} and found {FACTION} there first, have decided the colony is easier pickings.

texts.li: The wreck of {NAME} has been picked clean, down to the deck plates. {FACTION} took the lion's share, and they remember the colony's part in it.\n\nThe valley where it fell will be full of bent metal for years.

li.chronicle: The wreck of {NAME} was salvaged; {FACTION} remember the colony's part.

texts.li: The last of the salvagers have left the wreck of {NAME}. What's left in the valley is too heavy to move or too bent to sell.

li.chronicle: The wreck of {NAME} was picked clean.
